10.1002_adma.72026: Self-Healing Perovskites with Dendrimers In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.202512410), Min Jae Ko and co-workers present a dendrimer-based self-healing strategy for perovskite solar cells. The dendrimer, with its tree-like architecture and multi-functional branches, captures volatile species released during the moisture-induced decomposition of perovskite. By acting as a volatile reservoir, it enables reversible self-healing, allowing the perovskite film to restore its pristine structure through multiple degradation cycles.
10.1002_smll.202514662: O3‐type layered cathodes have attracted extensive attention due to their high reversible capacity and sufficient sodium‐ion utilization. However, induced by continuous phase transitions, O3‐type cathodes generally suffer from severe structural degradation and performance deterioration during the charge/discharge process. In response to this challenge, the single‐crystalline O3/P2 biphasic layered cathodes (O3/P2‐NNMO) were realized by a facile solvent‐regulated strategy. The characterization results indicated that O3/P2‐NNMO cathodes are endowed with the favorable surface chemistry environments contributed by low surface residual‐sodium impurities and high Mn 4+ /Mn 3+ proportion. Importantly, P2 phase was inter‐grown into O3‐type phase to form an interlock structure in a single‐crystalline O3/P2‐NNMO particle, which relieves the phase transitions to remarkably reduces lattice variation. The stable surface structure and reinforced bulk lattice cooperatively strengthen the cycling stability of cathodes. As expected, O3/P2‐NNMO cathodes deliver a high reversible capacity of 117.2 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C (14 mA g −1 ), and excellent cycling stability with a capacity retention of 75% after 100 cycles at 1 C. Also, the fast Na + migration pathway provided by P2 phase significantly promotes the Na + diffusion kinetics and interfacial charge transfer in O3/P2‐NNMO cathodes, enabling a superior rate capability. This work provides a new design idea for advanced layered cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries.
10.1016_j.jhydrol.2026.135439: Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging environmental concern driven by extensive plastic use and inadequate waste management. As rivers act as major transport pathways and temporary sinks, reducing MPs loads within them can limit their transfer into the food chain. This study examines the ability of groynes, structures originally designed for flow and erosion control, to trap non-buoyant MPs. Ten configurations formed from pairwise combinations of four common groyne geometries were tested using MPs (of equivalent diameter deq = 2.29 mm) of two densities (ρs = 1.08 and 1.11 g/cm³) under subcritical turbulent flow in a recirculating flume. A particle tracking model was applied to derive particle trajectories, trapping efficiencies, and retention zones. It was observed that MPs entered the groyne field from the downstream end and formed a major gyre. All scenarios retained > 6% of particles during the test period. When both groynes shared the same shape, upstream-facing inclined groynes exhibited the greatest trapping potential, achieving retention rates up to 20.7 ± 3.7%. Straight and T-shaped groynes had lower entrainment but higher stability, with less than 3% escape. In cases where the upstream groyne was straight and the downstream geometry was varied, particle escape was negligible, with downstream repelling groynes consistently trapping more MPs than other configurations. Particle density had minimal effect on entrainment, though lighter MPs exhibited lower escape and smaller retention zones, reflecting sensitivity to vertical flow dynamics within the groyne field. The study highlights groynes’ potential role in mitigating riverine plastic pollution.
10.1016_j.trd.2026.105382: This study investigates the current and projected cost-competitiveness of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) against conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) counterparts in the Indonesian market by examining their total cost of ownership (TCO). We find that existing policies have made BEVs and E2Ws purchased in 2024 already more cost-competitive than ICE vehicles and two-wheelers across all categories. However, in the absence of current tax concessions and subsidies, long-range E2Ws would not achieve cost-competitiveness over their internal combustion counterparts until 2027. The TCO of electric vehicles is also sensitive to battery-pack cost and cost projections as well as to the annual distance travelled. Despite their cost-competitiveness, the uptake of BEVs and E2Ws is still limited in Indonesia. Policy action may be focused on establishing the necessary support infrastructure to enable uptake.
10.1039_d5gc06342f: The CO 2 -induced r-ZnO-pc/Zn-CO 2 electrode demonstrated exceptional performance for the eCO 2 RR-to-syngas conversion, delivering a peak FE CO of 98.6% and a tunable syngas ratio of 0.8 to 12.5.
10.1039_d6cc03412h: A comparative study of two molecular cobalt catalysts for the nitrite reduction reaction revealed that the bipyridine-dioxime complex (1) outperforms the bis-pyridine-dioxime analog (2). The enhanced activity of 1 is attributed to the superior stabilization of catalytic intermediates by the bipyridine ligand framework.
